sections.h2: What should a seller know about Englewood, NJ before listing?
sections.html:
Englewood is a small Bergen County city of 4.93 square miles with 30,035 residents, and it enforces a Certificate of Continued Occupancy on every sale of a one, two or multi-family house. The inspection is short, but the permit check that comes first can take longer than the visit itself, so begin early.

Census figures for 2020 to 2024 show a median owner-occupied home value of $544,100, median household income of $102,571, and 54.5 percent of homes owner occupied. The city has 11,274 households and 5,951 people per square mile,.

sections.h2: How does the Englewood Certificate of Continued Occupancy work?
sections.html:
City Ordinance 85-40, in Chapter 9 of the Revised General Ordinances, says a seller must receive a CCO before ownership transfers. New construction and buildings the state inspects, such as hotels and rooming houses, are outside it. The city's stated purpose is to check safety and to hand the new owner information about fire and occupancy rules.

  1. Once you have a buyer, the seller or agent visits the Englewood Municipal Building at 2-10 North Van Brunt Street, second floor, and tells the Building Department about the sale.
  2. Any open permits for work on the property must be closed out before an inspection can be scheduled.
  3. The application asks for the property address, owner and buyer contact details, the buyer's present address (or a mailing address for an LLC or corporation), and the number of people living there before and after the sale.
  4. You pay the fee to the City of Englewood and the inspector visits.
  5. The certificate is passed to the buyer at closing.

Selling without a CCO risks fines and delays at the closing table.

sections.h2: What does the inspector check, and what does it cost?
sections.html:
Englewood CCO fees and inspector checks
ItemDetail
Fee, one or two family house$150
Fee, multi-family building$250
StructureWalls, floors, ceilings, stairs and rails intact and safe
Smoke detectorAt least one working unit on each level of living space
Carbon monoxide detectorAt least one working unit within 10 feet of each bedroom
Fire extinguisherOne ABC type, 2 to 10 pounds, within 10 feet of each kitchen

Source: City of Englewood, Certificate of Continued Occupancy letter to sellers and agents.

The same visit looks for illegal installations, illegal apartments and illegally rented rooms.

sections.h2: What happens if the inspector finds an illegal unit or unpermitted work?
sections.html:
The owner has to remove the extra unit, which means cutting off utility service and removing the added kitchen and bathroom. The certificate issues only after a second inspection confirms the work is done and the code is met. Work that needed a permit and did not get one must go through the Building Department first.

If you suspect an old basement apartment or an attic conversion has no paperwork, talk to the Building Department before you accept a contract. Raising it early leaves time to renegotiate before the closing date is fixed.

sections.h2: What is Englewood like, and who buys here?
sections.html:
Englewood borders Bergenfield, Englewood Cliffs, Fort Lee, Leonia, Teaneck and Tenafly, and Highwood is an unincorporated community inside its lines. The area was part of the English Neighborhood during the colonial era, and street names such as Brinckerhoff, Van Brunt, Lydecker, Demarest and Van Nostrand recall the Dutch, Huguenot and English families who settled it.

  • Four of the city's five National Register sites are houses on Grand Avenue: the Benson, Demarest, Lydecker and Demott-Westervelt houses. The fifth is St. Paul's Episcopal Church on Engle Street.
  • Flat Rock Brook is a 150 acre preserve on Van Nostrand Avenue with 3.6 miles of trails, and MacKay Park on North Van Brunt Street has a pool, rink and athletic fields.
  • Englewood Hospital sits on Engle Street.

Residents in the Census data are 32.2 percent White alone, 20.4 percent Black alone, 14.9 percent Asian alone, and 33.5 percent Hispanic or Latino, and 36.4 percent of people were born abroad.

sections.h2: What do Englewood owners and renters pay each month?
sections.html:
Census estimates for 2020 to 2024 put median selected monthly owner costs at $3,464 with a mortgage and $1,500 or more without one. Median gross rent is $1,977, higher than in Elizabeth or Egg Harbor Township. Per capita income is $59,017, and 9.2 percent of residents live in poverty.

  • Retail sales reached $49,278 per resident in 2022, the highest of the four towns.
  • Health care and social assistance receipts totaled about $1.6 billion in 2022, reflecting the hospital on Engle Street.
  • Adults 25 and older with a bachelor's degree or higher make up 46.5 percent.

Compare your carrying costs against those medians when deciding how long to wait for an offer.

The Lenape, of the turtle clan, lived here first; a population of about 2,000 had dwindled to 50 by 1832. Henry Hudson's 1607 voyage let the Netherlands claim the watershed, but settlement picked up only after England took New Netherland in 1664. The Garret Lydecker House on Grand Avenue dates to 1808.

Whatever your house's age, the CCO inspector reads any addition or conversion as a permit question.

sections.h2: How do commuting and schools factor into an Englewood sale?
sections.html:
Interstate 95 clips the city for 0.43 miles near the Leonia line. Routes 4 and 93 and county routes 501 and 505 carry local traffic. NJ Transit bus 166 runs to the Port Authority Bus Terminal, while routes 171, 175, 178 and 186 serve the George Washington Bridge Bus Station, and Rockland Coaches also runs to Port Authority. Passenger trains on the Erie Northern Branch served Englewood from 1859 until 1966, and a proposed light rail extension would add stops at Englewood Route 4, Englewood Town Center and the hospital. Mean travel time to work is 30.9 minutes.

The Englewood Public School District had 2,955 students in five schools for 2023-24, from the D. A. Quarles Early Childhood Center to Dwight Morrow High School, which also takes students from Englewood Cliffs. Bergen County students can apply to the Bergen County Academies and other county technical programs, and the city has the Englewood on the Palisades Charter School.

sections.h2: What are the state steps at the deed, and where does it get recorded?
sections.html:
Bergen County's Clerk acts as the recording officer for deeds, mortgages and liens. The state charges the seller a realty transfer fee on the deed, and any price above $350,000 uses a higher schedule: for example, $4.80 per $500 on the slice between $200,000 and $550,000. Sales above $1,000,000 add a graduated percent fee that starts at 1 percent.

A resident seller signs the state's GIT/REP-3 form for recording, and nonresident sellers use GIT/REP-1 or GIT/REP-2 unless a stated assurance applies. For a tax assessment challenge, the county board of taxation must receive your petition by April 1, or May 1 where a revaluation or reassessment took place.

faqs.q: Do I need a CCO to sell a house in Englewood?
faqs.a: Yes. City Ordinance 85-40 requires a Certificate of Continued Occupancy for one, two and multi-family houses before ownership changes hands.

faqs.q: How much is the Englewood CCO inspection?
faqs.a: $150 for a one or two family home and $250 for a multi-family building, paid to the City of Englewood with the application.

faqs.q: What does the Englewood inspector look at for fire safety?
faqs.a: A working smoke detector on each level, a working carbon monoxide detector within 10 feet of bedrooms, and an ABC extinguisher of 2 to 10 pounds within 10 feet of the kitchen.

faqs.q: Where in Englewood do I start the CCO process?
faqs.a: At the Building Department, second floor of the Municipal Building, 2-10 North Van Brunt Street. Have the buyer's name, phone and address ready, and close out any open permits first.

faqs.q: How many people live in Englewood?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 30,035 residents for July 1, 2025, compared with 29,308 in the 2020 census.
